name: The homage World (unnamed)
parent: the shared universe (with Cian and Kares Prime)
homage_of: The United States, Great Migration through 2026 (thematic, not technological)

locational_claims.claim: A separate World within the same universe as Cian, not a Dimension and not a region of Cian; follows the Kares Prime precedent: a distinct, physically reachable planet.
Travel between worlds is available in-fiction, so the Great Migration homage can be literal migration between worlds.
Firmly pre-industrial: no engines beyond the Hymn-Engine/Meridian Engine, no firearms, no broadcast media; criers and hand-copied broadsheets instead.
The Sealbound Directorate does not operate here; a patrol in Taifa II was corrected from SBD to "the claimed land's hostile neighbors" as a world-bleed fix.
Homage-era survivors live long enough to become ancient veterans who reinforce Book 1 on Cian.

mention_count_basis: whole corpus (all Chronicle files incl. headers/notes + ledger statements), pattern: homage World|homage world|separate World
notes: No in-fiction proper name exists for this planet anywhere in canon. No sky, moon, climate, continent or ocean facts are locked.

name: Crossing between the homage World and Cian (mechanism undefined)

locational_claims.claim: Travel between worlds exists, "as it already is for Lauris" (her route ran Vask Olmedrin orbital trade-point to the Kesmara orbital descent station on Cian).
Kanja appears in every territory as an unnamed guest, but no Chronicle shows him arriving from Cian; Xaragua II has him "three days making his way toward that table" in Xaragua.
Xaragua I: "He was not dressed for Xaragua's coast"; leaves "in the direction of whatever coast next needed a body."
The only depiction of an homage-World figure on Cian (Ogoun Xarey at Maw-15) was withdrawn.

mention_count_basis: not countable (no named mechanism exists)
notes: Gap: no named port, gate, station or vessel; no arrival point on either side; no transit time. Needed before the Atlas can draw a universe-level link.
